entities.name: Apollodorus of Pergamon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Apollodorus of Pergamon (unknown–21 BCE) was a renowned ancient Greek rhetorician whose work shaped the development of rhetoric in the Hellenistic period.

Born in Pergamon, a city-state in modern-day Turkey, Apollodorus rose to prominence as a teacher and writer, producing a comprehensive treatise on rhetoric that became the foundation of a prominent school of thought.

His work not only influenced the art of rhetoric but also had a profound impact on the intellectual landscape of the ancient world, with his ideas transmitted through the centuries and studied by notable figures such as the Roman statesman Cicero.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, Apollodorus of Pergamon remains an important figure in the history of rhetoric and communication, with his contributions continuing to inspire scholars and writers to this day.

Theodorus of Gadara, who emerged as a rival to Apollodorus, also left a lasting mark on the history of rhetoric, paving the way for future developments in the field.
